paragraphs.source_en: Hope—only now... Now there remain only some relics; Pitiful heart of mine... How can it teach me how to bury and cover you? Hope, I touch the cruel wound your life became, on this cold, silent winter night, with whom am I to decide your burial? Bury you in the autumn woods, by a secluded ravine, if you will. In the morning, listen to the lively chime of the spring; at dusk, rest against the soft fragrance of pine and grass. I gather a basketful of crimson leaves, maple leaves of autumn, withered and damp with dew, to lay over your new grave, that beautiful Hope may sleep forever. I sing a dim, sorrowful song, and let it blend with the autumn forest’s own sound. Clear tears, like droplets of cold dew, are scattered over the new, cold grave. I hold in my arms your cold, broken garments, and grieve for the life you lived— an unfortunate mother of love, recalling the hardships of years of nurturing. Still, I cannot bear to bury you. Hope—my life and my light! Like that princess gone mad with love, holding close the cold corpse of her beloved. Dreamlike, blurred, as if floating, in the end, who remains, and who perishes? Who is it that sings this sorrowful dirge, O Hope! You and I—who, in the end, burys whom? "Beauty is the immortal radiance of the human world," whether it be life, or hope. Even so, cold bones may still emit a divine light of life; why then ask the red leaves of autumn woods to bury you? Written on 24 January 1923.

paragraphs.source_zh:
希望，只如今……

如今只剩些遺骸；

可憐，我的心……

卻教我如何埋掩？

希望，我撫摩著

你慘變的創傷，

在這冷默的冬夜

誰與我商量埋葬？

埋你在秋林之中，

幽澗之邊，你願否，

朝餐泉樂的琤瑽，

暮偎著松茵香柔？

我收拾一筐的紅葉，

露凋秋傷的楓葉，

舖蓋在你新墳之上，──

長眠著美麗的希望！

我唱一支慘淡的歌，

與秋林的秋聲相和；

滴滴涼露似的清淚，

灑遍了清冷的新墓！

我手抱你冷殘的衣裳，

悽懷你生前的經過──

一個遭不幸的愛母

回想一場撫養的辛苦。

我又捨不得將你埋葬，

希望，我的生命與光明！

像那個情瘋了的公主，

緊摟住她愛人的冷屍！

夢境似的惝恍，

畢竟是誰存與誰亡？

是誰在悲唱，希望！

你，我，是誰替誰埋葬？

「美是人間不死的光芒，」

不論是生命，或是希望；

便冷骸也發生命的神光，

何必問秋林紅葉去埋葬？

一九二三年一月二十四日作
